Chats, documents, tasks, invoices, and models use app-private storage. Deleting a chat does not delete other data. Clearing app storage removes local data; shared files and submitted reports are separate.
Camera permission is required to take photos.
Location access supplies coordinates to the weather provider to retrieve your forecast. Coordinates may be cached briefly on this device; they are not sent to our own servers by the weather feature.
Contacts access searches names and email addresses locally. If you choose to draft, share, or send those details to another app or a confirmed remote tool, that destination receives them.
Calendar access reads local event data. Creating events opens your calendar app, which may sync events using its own account and network settings.

Microphone access measures sound locally or supports voice input. Voice input uses your Android speech provider and requests offline recognition, but the provider may use a network service. Review your speech provider settings before dictating sensitive information.

Standard Gemma 4 models are optimized for mobile. Smaller models often use less memory and may respond faster, with tradeoffs on complex tasks.

Gemma 4: Standard mobile variants are optimized for on-device use. E2B is the smaller option; E4B needs more memory. Web and other specialized conversions can have different capabilities.

Smaller models: Often lighter and faster, but can be less reliable for complex reasoning, coding, and tool use. Accuracy differences depend on the task.

Spark X2.6: The current INT8 variant runs on CPU and may be slower than Gemma 4, despite a similar parameter count.

Actual speed depends on your device, model conversion, acceleration, and conversation length. Compare models using the same task.

I can answer questions, help with writing, explain and debug code across languages and platforms, summarize, translate, brainstorm, and help plan tasks. In this app I can search imported text and Markdown documents with /docs, analyze attached images with a compatible vision model, search the web, check weather, manage tasks, and scan or import invoices and receipts. I can read live device sensor readings when supported and permitted, and open sensor screens for radar, stud finder or metal detector, spirit level, light, proximity, and sound. I can also copy or share text, open links, maps and installed apps, draft email, create calendar events, and check local model information. With /mcp and an HTTPS server endpoint, I can discover and call remote tools with your confirmation; servers requiring sign-in or API tokens are not supported yet. Image generation is not available in this build. With a compatible vision model, I can describe attached images and help extract text from them.

Yes. I can read live device sensors like ambient light, pressure, battery and thermal status, accelerometer motion, gyroscope rotation, compass heading, proximity, posture, flatness, metal or magnetic field strength, and microphone-based ambient noise when microphone permission is granted. I can also open dedicated sensor screens: /sensors for the full dashboard, /stud for stud finder or metal detector, /level for spirit level, /light for light meter, and /proximity for proximity detection.
